title: Acts Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 11.

questions.question: In Acts 11, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Peter was in the city of Joppa praying
The apostles and brethren in Judaea heard that the Gentiles had received the word
Peter saw a vision of a great sheet let down from heaven
Peter contended with those of the circumcision
questions.correctAnswer: The apostles and brethren in Judaea heard that the Gentiles had received the word
questions.explanation: Acts 11:1 states that the apostles and brethren that were in Judaea heard that the Gentiles had received the word of God, which is the earliest event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: Who contended with Peter when he came up to Jerusalem?
options: Those that were of the circumcision
questions.correctAnswer: Those that were of the circumcision
questions.explanation: Acts 11:2 states that those that were of the circumcision contended with Peter when he came up to Jerusalem.

questions.question: What was the reason given by those who contended with Peter?
options: He had preached to the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: He ate with men uncircumcised
questions.explanation: Acts 11:3 says they contended with Peter saying, 'Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.'

questions.question: What did Peter do to explain his actions to those who contended with him?
options: He rehearsed the matter from the beginning
He apologized and promised not to do it again
He called a council to discuss it
questions.correctAnswer: He rehearsed the matter from the beginning
questions.explanation: Acts 11:4 states that Peter rehearsed the matter from the beginning, and expounded it by order unto them.

questions.question: Where was Peter when he saw the vision of a vessel descending like a great sheet?
questions.correctAnswer: Joppa
questions.explanation: Acts 11:5 states that Peter was in the city of Joppa praying when he saw the vision.

questions.question: What did Peter see in the vision descending from heaven?
options: A great sheet let down by four corners
questions.correctAnswer: A great sheet let down by four corners
questions.explanation: Acts 11:5 describes the vision of a certain vessel descending as a great sheet let down from heaven by four corners.

questions.question: What kinds of creatures did Peter see in the vision?
options: Fourfooted beasts, wild beasts, creeping things, and fowls of the air
questions.correctAnswer: Fourfooted beasts, wild beasts, creeping things, and fowls of the air
questions.explanation: Acts 11:6 states that Peter saw fourfooted beasts of the earth, wild beasts, creeping things, and fowls of the air in the vision.

questions.question: What command did Peter hear in the vision?
options: Go, Peter; preach to the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: Arise, Peter; slay and eat
questions.explanation: Acts 11:7 states that Peter heard a voice saying unto him, 'Arise, Peter; slay and eat.'

questions.question: How did Peter initially respond to the command to eat?
options: He said, 'I will wait for a sign'
He said, 'Not so, Lord: for nothing common or unclean hath at any time entered into my mouth.'
questions.correctAnswer: He said, 'Not so, Lord: for nothing common or unclean hath at any time entered into my mouth.'
questions.explanation: Acts 11:8 records Peter's response saying, 'Not so, Lord: for nothing common or unclean hath at any time entered into my mouth.'

questions.question: What was the voice's reply to Peter's refusal to eat?
options: What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common
Go and ask for further instructions
questions.correctAnswer: What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common
questions.explanation: Acts 11:9 states the voice answered Peter, 'What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.'

questions.question: How many times was the vision repeated to Peter?
questions.correctAnswer: Three times
questions.explanation: Acts 11:10 states that this was done three times and all were drawn up again into heaven.

questions.question: The apostles and brethren in Judaea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 11:1 explicitly states that the apostles and brethren that were in Judaea heard that the Gentiles had received the word of God.

questions.question: Peter was in a trance when he saw the vision of the great sheet descending from heaven.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 11:5 states that Peter was in a trance when he saw the vision.

questions.question: Peter was criticized for refusing to eat with the uncircumcised.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 11:3 states that Peter was contended with because he went in to men uncircumcised and did eat with them, not for refusing to eat with them.

questions.question: The vision Peter saw included a ladder reaching from earth to heaven.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 11:5-10 describe a vision of a great sheet let down from heaven with various animals, but there is no mention of a ladder.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who were the three men that came to the house where Peter was, as mentioned in Acts 11:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Men sent from Caesarea
questions.explanation: Acts 11:11 states that three men had come to the house where Peter was, sent from Caesarea.

questions.question: What does Acts 11:14 promise will happen if someone calls for Simon Peter as instructed in Acts 11:13?
options: They and all their house shall be saved
They will receive a great reward
They will be healed of their sickness
questions.correctAnswer: They and all their house shall be saved
questions.explanation: Acts 11:14 promises that Simon Peter shall tell words by which the person and all his house shall be saved, following the instruction in Acts 11:13.

questions.question: What event caused Peter to remember the Lord's words about baptism with the Holy Ghost?
options: The Holy Ghost falling on the Gentiles
The arrival of the six brethren
The vision of the great sheet
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Ghost falling on the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Acts 11:15 says as Peter began to speak, the Holy Ghost fell on them, which led him to remember the Lord's words about baptism with the Holy Ghost in Acts 11:16.

questions.question: How do Acts 11:16 and Acts 11:17 together explain Peter's reaction to the Gentiles receiving the Holy Ghost?
options: Peter recognized that God gave the same gift to Gentiles, so he could not oppose God
Peter decided to reject the Gentiles because they were uncircumcised
Peter was confused and sought advice from the apostles
Peter thought the Gentiles needed to be baptized with water first
questions.correctAnswer: Peter recognized that God gave the same gift to Gentiles, so he could not oppose God
questions.explanation: Acts 11:16 recalls the promise of baptism with the Holy Ghost, and Acts 11:17 explains that since God gave them the same gift as to the believers, Peter could not withstand God.

questions.question: What was the reaction of those who heard Peter's account about Gentiles receiving repentance unto life?
options: They held their peace and glorified God
questions.correctAnswer: They held their peace and glorified God
questions.explanation: Acts 11:18 states that when they heard these things, they held their peace and glorified God, acknowledging that God granted repentance to the Gentiles.

questions.question: Where did the scattered believers go after the persecution arising about Stephen, as described in Acts 11:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Phenice, Cyprus, and Antioch
questions.explanation: Acts 11:19 says that those scattered traveled as far as Phenice, Cyprus, and Antioch preaching the word to Jews only.

questions.question: Who were the ones that spoke to the Grecians in Antioch, preaching the Lord Jesus, according to Acts 11:20?
questions.correctAnswer: Men of Cyprus and Cyrene
questions.explanation: Acts 11:20 identifies that men of Cyprus and Cyrene, when they came to Antioch, spoke to the Grecians and preached the Lord Jesus.

questions.question: According to Acts 11:12, why did Peter go with the men sent from Caesarea?
options: Because the Spirit bade him go with them, nothing doubting
Because he wanted to preach to the Gentiles
Because he sought to verify the vision by himself
Because he was commanded by the apostles
questions.correctAnswer: Because the Spirit bade him go with them, nothing doubting
questions.explanation: Acts 11:12 explains that the Spirit instructed Peter to go with the men without doubting.

questions.question: What is the significance of the angel's message in Cornelius's house as described in Acts 11:13?
options: To send men to Joppa to call for Simon Peter
To prepare a feast for the apostles
To instruct Cornelius to fast and pray
questions.correctAnswer: To send men to Joppa to call for Simon Peter
questions.explanation: Acts 11:13 describes that the angel instructed Cornelius to send men to Joppa and call for Simon Peter.

questions.question: How does Acts 11:15 illustrate the continuation of the Holy Ghost's work compared to the beginning of the Christian movement?
options: The Holy Ghost fell on the Gentiles as it did on the apostles at the beginning
The Holy Ghost was withheld until after baptism
The Holy Ghost was only given to Jewish believers
The Holy Ghost caused confusion among the listeners
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Ghost fell on the Gentiles as it did on the apostles at the beginning
questions.explanation: Acts 11:15 states that as Peter spoke, the Holy Ghost fell on them just as it had at the beginning upon the apostles, showing God's inclusive work.

questions.question: What lesson about obedience can be learned from Peter’s response to the Spirit’s instruction in Acts 11:12?
options: Obeying the Spirit without doubting leads to fulfilling God’s plan
It is wise to question the Spirit before acting
Obedience depends on the approval of others
Actions should wait until all doubts are resolved
questions.correctAnswer: Obeying the Spirit without doubting leads to fulfilling God’s plan
questions.explanation: Acts 11:12 highlights Peter’s immediate and unquestioning obedience to the Spirit, which was crucial for God’s plan to unfold.

questions.question: Why was Peter unable to withstand God’s work among the Gentiles according to Acts 11:17?
options: Because God gave them the same gift as to the Jewish believers
Because he was afraid of persecution
questions.correctAnswer: Because God gave them the same gift as to the Jewish believers
questions.explanation: Acts 11:17 states that since God gave the Gentiles the same spiritual gift as the Jewish believers, Peter could not oppose God's work.

questions.question: What can Christians learn about God’s inclusiveness from the events in Acts 11:18?
options: God grants repentance and life to Gentiles as well as Jews
God favors only those of Jewish descent
Repentance is limited to those within Jerusalem
Salvation requires strict adherence to the law
questions.correctAnswer: God grants repentance and life to Gentiles as well as Jews
questions.explanation: Acts 11:18 shows that those who heard Peter glorified God for granting repentance unto life to the Gentiles, indicating God’s inclusive plan.

questions.question: True or False: According to Acts 11:20, the men of Cyprus and Cyrene preached only to the Jews in Antioch.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 11:20 specifies that these men preached to the Grecians (Gentiles), not only to Jews.

questions.question: True or False: Acts 11:18 highlights that God has granted repentance unto life to the Gentiles.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 11:18 clearly states that God has granted repentance unto life to the Gentiles, as acknowledged by those who heard Peter.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 11.

questions.question: What was the result of the hand of the Lord being with them?
options: A great number believed and turned unto the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: A great number believed and turned unto the Lord
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Acts 11:21 states that 'the hand of the Lord was with them: and a great number believed, and turned unto the Lord.'

questions.question: Who did the church in Jerusalem send to Antioch?
questions.correctAnswer: Barnabas
questions.explanation: Acts 11:22 indicates that 'they sent forth Barnabas, that he should go as far as Antioch.'

questions.question: What did Barnabas see when he arrived in Antioch?
questions.correctAnswer: The grace of God
questions.explanation: Barnabas was glad because he 'had seen the grace of God' as stated in Acts 11:23.

questions.question: What was Barnabas known for?
options: Being a good man and full of the Holy Ghost
questions.correctAnswer: Being a good man and full of the Holy Ghost
questions.explanation: Acts 11:24 describes Barnabas as 'a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith.'

questions.question: What significant name were the disciples first called in Antioch?
questions.correctAnswer: Christians
questions.explanation: Acts 11:26 mentions that 'the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.'

questions.question: What did Agabus predict in Antioch?
options: A great dearth throughout all the world
questions.correctAnswer: A great dearth throughout all the world
questions.explanation: Acts 11:28 states that Agabus signified 'that there should be great dearth throughout all the world.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'kletos' in Acts 11:26 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Called
questions.explanation: 'Kletos' translates to 'called,' indicating the name given to the disciples.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used when describing Barnabas's character?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The description of Barnabas's character includes 'good man' and 'full of the Holy Ghost,' creating an inclusio around his positive traits.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of sending aid to those in need as seen in Acts 11:29?
questions.correctAnswer: Galatians 6:2
questions.explanation: Galatians 6:2 states, 'Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ,' echoing the theme of providing relief.

questions.question: Which other passage fulfills the theme of the Gentiles receiving the word of God as in Acts 11:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Ephesians 3:6
questions.explanation: Ephesians 3:6 speaks of the Gentiles being fellow heirs, fulfilling the theme of the Gentiles receiving God's word.

questions.question: What comes before the mention of Barnabas seeking Saul in Acts 11:25?
options: The church in Jerusalem sent Barnabas
Barnabas saw the grace of God
questions.correctAnswer: Barnabas saw the grace of God
questions.explanation: Acts 11:24 discusses Barnabas's actions and observations before he sought Saul.

questions.question: In Acts 11:27, who came from Jerusalem to Antioch?
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets
questions.explanation: Acts 11:27 specifically states that 'prophets from Jerusalem came unto Antioch.'

questions.question: The word 'dearth' in Acts 11:28 signifies what?
questions.correctAnswer: Famine
questions.explanation: 'Dearth' refers to famine or scarcity, as indicated by Agabus's prophecy.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples were called Christians first in Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: This statement is false because Acts 11:26 states that 'the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.'

questions.question: True or False: Barnabas was full of the Holy Ghost and of faith.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This statement is true as Acts 11:24 describes Barnabas as 'a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith.'

theological.title: Acts Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 11:9 teach about God's nature in relation to ceremonial law?
options: God redefines what is ceremonially clean and unclean
God maintains the immutability of ceremonial law
God requires strict adherence to Jewish customs
questions.correctAnswer: God redefines what is ceremonially clean and unclean
questions.explanation: Acts 11:9 shows the voice from heaven telling Peter not to call common what God has cleansed, indicating God’s authority to redefine ceremonial cleanness.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the baptism of the Holy Spirit is taught in Acts 11:16?
options: Holy Spirit baptism is a gift distinct from water baptism
Water baptism imparts the Holy Spirit automatically
The Holy Spirit baptism is symbolic only
Baptism by the Holy Spirit was only for the apostles
questions.correctAnswer: Holy Spirit baptism is a gift distinct from water baptism
questions.explanation: Acts 11:16 contrasts John's water baptism with the baptism by the Holy Spirit, showing they are distinct gifts.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the inclusion of Gentiles in salvation is taught in Acts 11:18?
options: God grants repentance and life to Gentiles as well as Jews
Gentiles must first become Jews to be saved
Salvation is limited to the circumcised
questions.correctAnswer: God grants repentance and life to Gentiles as well as Jews
questions.explanation: Acts 11:18 states the church glorified God because He granted repentance to life to the Gentiles, affirming their inclusion.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 11:5 specifically demonstrate through Peter's vision?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Acts 11:5 shows God sovereignly revealing His will to Peter through a vision, directing the mission to Gentiles.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Acts 11:21 by the statement 'The hand of the Lord was with them'?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Acts 11:21 describes God's providential support for the missionaries, enabling many to believe.

questions.question: How does Acts 11:26 connect with the broader biblical theme of the identity of believers?
options: It marks the first use of the term 'Christian', defining a new identity in Christ
It reinforces the exclusive identity of Jews as God's people
It indicates a rejection of Jesus as Messiah
It highlights a return to Old Testament priestly titles
questions.correctAnswer: It marks the first use of the term 'Christian', defining a new identity in Christ
questions.explanation: Acts 11:26 indicates the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch, establishing a new identity based on Christ.

questions.question: In what way does the sending of relief to Judea in Acts 11:29–30 fulfill an Old Testament theme?
options: It fulfills the theme of communal care and support among God's people
It fulfills the requirement of temple sacrifices
It emphasizes separation of Gentiles from Jews
It rejects the notion of mutual aid
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the theme of communal care and support among God's people
questions.explanation: Acts 11:29–30 shows the disciples practicing mutual aid, reflecting Old Testament principles of caring for the needy in the covenant community.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 11:15 and 11:16 teach about the work of the Holy Spirit in salvation?
options: The Holy Spirit's work confirms the inclusion of Gentiles and fulfills Jesus’ promise of Spirit baptism
The Spirit's work is limited to Jewish believers only
Spirit baptism replaces faith in Christ
The Spirit's work is purely symbolic
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit's work confirms the inclusion of Gentiles and fulfills Jesus’ promise of Spirit baptism
questions.explanation: Acts 11:15–16 shows the Holy Spirit falling on Gentiles as on the apostles, fulfilling Jesus’ promise of baptism with the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 11:4 and 11:17 teach about human submission to divine revelation?
options: Believers must submit to God's sovereign will even when it challenges tradition
Human tradition always supersedes divine revelation
Divine revelation is optional in Christian life
God’s commands can be resisted by human authority
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must submit to God's sovereign will even when it challenges tradition
questions.explanation: Acts 11:4 recounts Peter's explanation of his vision and Acts 11:17 records his submission to God’s decision, even against Jewish tradition.

questions.question: What synthesis about the mission to the Gentiles is taught by combining Acts 11:20 and Acts 11:23?
options: The mission to Gentiles is empowered by the grace of God and the preaching of the gospel
The mission to Gentiles was initially rejected by all believers
Gentiles were evangelized without any divine support
The mission to Gentiles was a human initiative without God's involvement
questions.correctAnswer: The mission to Gentiles is empowered by the grace of God and the preaching of the gospel
questions.explanation: Acts 11:20 shows men preaching to the Grecians, and 11:23 highlights Barnabas encouraging believers upon seeing God’s grace, indicating divine empowerment.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Acts 11:1–18 supports a doctrine of salvation by works due to the emphasis on ritual cleanliness. What does Acts 11:1–18 actually teach?
options: It teaches salvation is by grace and the Spirit, not by ritual law
It teaches salvation requires strict observance of dietary laws
It teaches Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved
It teaches works of the law are the basis of salvation
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches salvation is by grace and the Spirit, not by ritual law
questions.explanation: Acts 11:1–18 shows Peter’s vision declaring all foods clean and the Spirit falling on Gentiles, emphasizing salvation by grace through the Spirit, not by law.

questions.question: What doctrine about prophetic ministry is taught in Acts 11:28?
options: Prophets are inspired by the Spirit to reveal future events
Prophecy is no longer active in the church
Prophetic messages are always immediate and local
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets are inspired by the Spirit to reveal future events
questions.explanation: Acts 11:28 records Agabus, a prophet, indicating by the Spirit a coming famine, demonstrating Spirit-inspired future revelation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God's granting of repentance to the Gentiles in Acts 11:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Acts 11:18 celebrates God granting repentance to Gentiles, showcasing His attribute of mercy extended beyond Israel.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 11:25 and 11:26 teach about the role of apostolic partnership in church planting and teaching?
options: Apostolic partnerships are essential for establishing and strengthening churches
Church planting is a solo endeavor without collaboration
Teaching is unnecessary once the church is planted
questions.correctAnswer: Apostolic partnerships are essential for establishing and strengthening churches
questions.explanation: Acts 11:25–26 shows Barnabas seeking Saul and together teaching the church for a year, highlighting the importance of partnership.

questions.question: How does Acts 11:12 demonstrate the attribute of divine guidance in the early church's mission?
options: The Spirit bade Peter to go with the men without doubt
The church acted independently of the Spirit's direction
Peter doubted and refused to go
Mission decisions were based on human reasoning alone
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit bade Peter to go with the men without doubt
questions.explanation: Acts 11:12 explicitly states the Spirit instructed Peter to accompany the men, showing divine guidance in mission.
